Petition under Section 166 & 140 of M.V. Act, 1988 for grant of compensation AWARD 1.

The present petition has been filed by the petitioners U/s 166 & 140 M.V.Act seeking compensation of Rs. 50,00,000/- alongwith interest @ 18% per annum from the date of filing of the present claim petition till its realization being legal representatives of deceased Sanjay Kumar on account of death of deceased who died in road traffic accident in question which occurred on 16.11.2014.

The petitioners also prayed for compensation for irreparable monetary loss, mental agony, loss of love and affection and future prospects plus all other heads of compensation as per entitlement, caused due to accidental death of deceased.
MACP Nos. 5617/16, FIR No. 1447/14; PS. Narela DOD: 10.01.2025 2.

The concise material facts relevant to decide the present claim petition as averred are that on 16.11.2014 at about 5:50 P.M., deceased namely Sanjay Kumar alongwith his son Amit (petitioner no. 2) were standing near Ghogha Community Hall, Ghogha Chowk, Village-Ghogha, Narela,
Delhi-39 when respondent no. 1, driver of Delhi Police Bus bearing No. DL-1PC-2586 reversed his Bus at a very fast speed rashly and negligently and crushed the deceased with rear tyre of the Bus.
The deceased was taken to SRHC Hospital where he was declared brought dead due to the injuries in the accident.
The deceased was about 35 years at the time of accident.
A case U/s. 279/304A IPC was registered at PS Narela vide FIR No. 1447/14 with regard to the accident in question.
The petitioners have claimed that the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of aforementioned offending vehicle which was allegedly being driven by respondent no.1/driver.
The offending vehicle was found to be owned by respondent no. 2 at the time of accident in question.

3. In their identical written statement, the respondent no. 1 and 2 i.e. driver and registered owner have claimed that the respondent no. 1 did not visit the place of accident on the date alleged as it was on government duty from 8:00 AM to 8:00 PM on 16.11.2014 and respondent no. 1 alongwith offending vehicle made his departure vide DD no. 13A dated 16.11.2014 for 3rd battalion, ITBP, PS Mundka, Delhi.

Respondent no. 1 has also stated that from there, he had gone to Pragati Maidan and at 2:00 PM he again started his journey from Pragati Maidan to Mundka to drop the force MACP Nos. 5617/16, FIR No. 1447/14; PS. Narela DOD: 10.01.2025 and was relieved from his duty at 8:00 PM from PS Mundka
due to which he spent his night in the police station itself.

It is further stated by him that on 17.11.2014 in the morning, he again left from Mundka to Pragati Maidan and from there to Kingsway Camp Police Line where he parked the vehicle in the vacant parking.
He further stated that he was having valid DL at the time of accident.
He stated that he has been falsely implicated at the instance of petitioner no. 2 who is not the son of deceased.
The same facts are also stated by respondent no. 2 in the WS.
They have denied the averments made in the claim petition and have prayed for its dismissal.

2 4.

From the pleadings of the parties and the documents, the following issues were framed vide order dated 07.08.2015:-
1) Whether the deceased Sanjay Kumar, suffered fatal injuries in road traffic accident on 16.11.2014 at about 5:50 pm, near Ghogha Community Hall, Ghogha Chowk,
Ghogha Village, Narela, Delhi within the jurisdiction of PS Narela, due to rashness and negligence on the part of driver /R-1, who was driving bus bearing registration no.
DL-1PC-2586, owned by R-2 ?

OPP.
2) Whether the LRs of deceased are entitled to any compensation, if so, to what amount and from whom?
OPP.
3) Relief.

5. To substantiate their claim, petitioners have examined three witnesses i.e. PW1 Roshni (wife of deceased), PW2 Amit (son of deceased) and PW-3 Sh. Rajesh Kumar and closed their evidence on 04.09.2018.

On the other hand, respondent no. 1 examined himself as R1W-1, R1W2 ASI MACP Nos. 5617/16, FIR No. 1447/14; PS. Narela DOD: 10.01.2025 Virender Singh (partly examined,
dropped vide order dated 14.11.2024), R1W-3 Sh. Yad Ram Vats, R1W-4 Sh. Shashi & R1W-5 Ct.
Pradeep.

RE was closed vide order dated 11.02.2021.
6.
This Tribunal has carefully perused the claim petition, evidence led by petitioners has been duly appreciated.
All documents and material relied upon perused and considered.
Arguments addressed by counsels for the petitioners and insurance company considered.
Legal position, both statutory and binding applicable precedents, has been appreciated.

The issue wise determination is as under:-
7.
The onus to prove, the aforesaid issue was placed on the petitioners.

To prove the said issue,
petitioners have examined PW-2 who stated on the lines of the claim petition.
In his cross-examination, he stated that his date of birth is 16.10.1992.
He denied the suggestion that his mother Roshni was not married with the deceased or that he is not the legal representative of the deceased.
He further stated that he called at 100 number at about 5:30-5:45 P.M. from his mobile which is registered in his name.
He also admitted that DD no. 34A mentions a mobile number which is not in his name.
He stated that several villagers had gathered at the spot after the accident and two of them were Arun and Ravish.
He further stated that police had reached the place of accident after about 30 minutes of his call.

He further stated that due to the MACP Nos. 5617/16, FIR No.
1447/14; PS. Narela DOD: 10.01.2025 accident, he had fallen down and he could not make efforts to stop the offending vehicle or to seek help from public persons to apprehend the driver.
He further stated that he did not sustain any injury due to the accident as the Bus had not hit him.
He further stated that he had fallen down due to the shock as the Bus had run over his father.

Roshni vs Kailash Kumar on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145064451/
3 8.
On the other hand, respondent no.1 has examined himself as R1W1.

In his affidavit in evidence,
he stated that on 16.11.2014, the alleged offending vehicle bearing no. DL-1PC-2586 was on Government Duty from 8.00a.m. to 8.00a.m. (24 hours) and he alongwith the vehicle made his departure vide DD no. 13A dated 16.11.2014 for third battalion, ITBP, PS Mundka, Delhi from where he had gone to Pragati Maidan.

He stated that when he reached near Mundka Metro Station, he met Yad Ram Vats and Sanjay Sharma at about 1.00p.m. and stated to them that he will return from Pragati Maidan to Mundka PS at about 4.00 to 4.30p.m. and asked them to meet there.
He stated that thereafter, he reached Pragati Maidan at 2.00p.m., dropped the force there.

He also met Ct.
Pradeep at Pragati Maidan and talked to him in his vehicle bearing no. DL-1PC-1626 and he again started his journey from Pragati Maidan to Mundka to drop the force.
He stated that in the meanwhile, he came to know that he forgot his mobile phone in the vehicle of Ct. Pradeep in Pragati Maidan.
He further stated that he was relieved from his duties at 8.00p.m. from PS Mundka and spend the night there.

In the morning of 17.11.2014, he again left from Mundka to Pragati Maidan to Kingsway Camp, Police Line where he parked his vehicle in the MACP Nos. 5617/16, FIR No.
1447/14; PS. Narela DOD: 10.01.2025 parking.
He stated that no accident took place with his vehicle on the alleged date, time and place.
He further stated that he had valid DL at the time of accident.
He also relied upon copy of his DL, Mark X and copies of DD No. 13A and 4A, Mark A and Mark B respectively.

In his cross examination by Ld. Counsel for the petitioners, he stated that he had filed complaint qua his false implication in the present case to his higher authorities on 17.11.2014 which is Ex.R1W1/P1.
He admitted that the offending vehicle was in his possession from 11.00a.m. of 16.11.2014 till 6.00a.m. of 17.11.2014.
He stated that he left alongwith his vehicle at 11.00a.m. on 16.11.2014 and reached Mundka at around 12.00noon where he stayed for about 30 to 45 minutes.
It is further stated that he had left with vehicle from Pragati Maidan at about 3.00p.m. alongwith staff of BSF in the vehicle towards Mundka.
He stated that since he was sitting alongwith Ct. Pradeep in his bus before leaving for Mundka, he had knowledge that his mobile phone was inadvertently left in the vehicle of Ct. Pradeep.
He further stated that he met Ct. Pradeep again when he had again gone to Pragati Maidan from Mundka on the same day.
It was then that Ct. Pradeep told him about his mobile phone being left in his vehicle.
He further stated that from there he again went back to Mundka at about 9.00p.m.

He further stated that he made about three visits to Pragati Maidan and back to Mundka on 16.11.2014 and the relevant entries regarding the said visit was being maintained in the Log Book Ex.R1W1/X1 of offending vehicle.
He admitted that the timings were not mentioned in the Log Book.

He further stated that MACP Nos. 5617/16, FIR No. 1447/14; PS. Narela DOD:
10.01.2025 Ct.
Pradeep had sent his mobile phone to him in the evening but he does not remember who brought it back to him.
He further stated that he had parked his vehicle at about 6.00a.m. on 17.11.2014 at Kingsway Camp.
He admitted that the show cause notice was received by him from the DCP office which is Ex.R1W1/X2 and that order dated 12.02.2015 Ex.R1W1/X3 was passed against him by the concerned DCP.
He further stated that he had lodged FIR against Sanjay S/o Mange Ram as he tried to kill him and that he was falsely implicated in the present case at the instance of Sanjay.

9. Respondent no.1 also examined R1W3 who stated in his affidavit in evidence that on 16.11.2014 he alongwith Sanjay Sharma were standing near Mundka Metro Station at about 1.00p.m. where they met the driver/ Kailash Kumar who informed them that he will return to PS Mundka at about 4.00 Roshni vs Kailash Kumar on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145064451/
4 to 4.30p.m.
He further stated that he alongwith Sanjay Sharma were present at PS Mundka at about 4.15p.m. to meet Kailash and at 4.30p.m.
Kailash was present there and they all stayed together till 6.00p.m. after which Kailash went to Pragati Maidan to drop the force.
In his cross examination by ld. Counsel for petitioner, he stated that on 16.11.2014 he was having weekly off.
He further stated that Kailash is his brother-in-law.
He further stated that he does not know whether Ct. Pradeep was present in PS Mundka when he was there alongwith Kailash.
He further stated that he never gave any statement to the IO during investigation or never filed any complaint regarding false implication of Kailash to the higher authority.
MACP Nos. 5617/16, FIR No. 1447/14; PS. Narela DOD: 10.01.2025 10.

Respondent no.1 also examined R1W4 who stated in his affidavit in evidence that on 16.11.2014 he was driving vehicle bearing no. DL-1C-5139 alongwith Kailash who was driving his vehicle bearing no. DL-1PC-2586 and they went to PS Mundka from Kingsway Camp at about 11.40a.m.
vide DD No. 13A dated 16.11.2014.
He further stated that he and Kailash reached PS Mundka at about 12.30p.m. and they went to Pragati Maidan from there.
He further stated that he alongwith Kailash stayed at PS Mundka and in the morning of next day i.e. 17.11.2014 he left alongwith Kailash from PS to Pragati Maidan.
In his cross examination, he stated that he was appointed by CHM to go with Kailash on 16.11.2014 vide a duty slip issued by CHM.
He further stated that they both started from Mundka Police Station around 1.00p.m. and took the route via Punjabi Bagh, Azadpur, ISBT and Pragati Maidan.
He also stated that they both did not stop their vehicles anywhere during the route and reached Pragati Maidan between 2.00/2.30p.m. and remained there for 35 to 40 minutes.

He further stated that they left Pragati Maidan at about 3.00p.m. and reached Mundka police station around 5.00p.m.
where they stayed till 8.00p.m.
He further stated that they made about two trips to Pragati Maidan on that day together.
He stated that he had not noticed whether Kailash was having his mobile phone between 5.00p.m. to 8.00p.m.
He stated that he knew Kailash being his colleague since last 6-7 years.
MACP Nos. 5617/16, FIR No. 1447/14; PS.
Narela DOD: 10.01.2025 11. R1W5 in his affidavit in evidence stated that Kailash reached Pragati Maidan at 2.00p.m. and dropped the force there where he met him.
He stated that Kailash forgot his phone in his vehicle before starting his journey from Pragati Maidan to Mundka.
He further stated that he returned the mobile phone to Kailash in the evening at about 8.30p.m.
In his cross examination, he stated that on 16.11.2014 he was doing his duty on his vehicle bearing no. DL-1PC-1626 to drop force from Bawana to Pragati Maidan.
He stated that the CRPF officials in his bus handed him the mobile phone in the evening and later on he came to know that it belongs to Kailash.

He stated that he remained with Kailash for about 20 to 25 minutes on that day and that the phone was identified by Kailash in the evening at around 8.00p.m. at Pragati Maidan where Kailash had gone to pick up officials and it was his second trip as told by Kailash to him.

Roshni vs Kailash Kumar on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145064451/
5 12.
From the testimony of PW2, it is seen that in his affidavit in evidence, he has stated that the accident was caused by bus bearing no. DL1PC-2586 while reversing the same and had crushed his father.
On the other hand, as per the chargesheet filed by IO, the call of accident was made on which the registration number of vehicle was not mentioned.

Further as per chargesheet statement of PW2 was recorded by IO in the first instance and he stated that he could not note down the Registration number of the offending vehicle which was a Delhi Police bus however identified the driver as respondent no.1 who was driving the bus and is known to the petitioners being the resident of the same village.

Upon the said statement on the basis MACP Nos. 5617/16, FIR No. 1447/14; PS. Narela DOD: 10.01.2025 of location of mobile number of driver Kailash he was charge sheeted by the IO and the vehicle on which he was on duty on the alleged date was made the offending vehicle.

Nowhere in his affidavit in evidence, PW2 has stated as to how he came to know the registration number of the offending vehicle, once he stated before the IO that he could not note down the registration number of the vehicle at the time of accident.

13. In the testimony of PW2 he has stated himself to be the eyewitness as he himself was present with the deceased at the time of accident however he did not disclose the registration number of the offending vehicle at the time of accident and only identified the driver as the person who caused the accident.

From the chargesheet filed by the IO, it is seen that he had clicked certain photographs of the CCTV footage( as clarified by IO later on that the CCTV footage was not seized , but only photograph were taken ) where in one bus is seen coming at 5:16 PM and leaving at 5:21 PM though the registration number of the bus is not clear, as stated by the IO.
Therefore, there is no other eyewitness or evidence on record to say that the accident was caused by the offending vehicle.
14. From the testimony of PW2, it is clear that he did not take his father to the hospital, despite stating that he was present the spot at the time of accident.
Further, he could not prove that he made any call to the police after the accident, despite having stated that he had called the PCR.
There is no record to show that any PCR call was made by him.
DD No. 34A at 5:57 MACP Nos. 5617/16, FIR No. 1447/14; PS. Narela DOD: 10.01.2025 PM
simply states that a dead body was lying on the road.
DD No. 35A at 6:05 pm states that accident injured serious.
Hence, neither FIR recorded on the statement of PW2 nor PCR calls disclosed the details of offending vehicle.
15. Further from the MLC of the deceased, it is seen that he was brought by the police van to the hospital and as per chargesheet, PW2 had also accompanied the deceased to the hospital.

However,
his presence at the hospital does not prove his presence at the time of accident as it has been reported by ASI Ramesh Chand that upon reaching the spot, many persons were found to have gathered at the spot, where the injured was also lying on the road and was bleeding from head.
In his testimony, PW2 also stated that though he was present along with his father, he did not sustain any injury at the time of accident.
In these circumstances, the presence of PW2 at the spot is highly doubtful and is not proved by him even on the basis of preponderance of probabilities during trial.
16. Further, as per the charge sheet, the location of the mobile phone of Driver Kailash was obtained on the basis of which the driver was made an accused in the charge sheet.

However, it is worth mentioning that the location of mobile phone does not prove the location of the offending vehicle,
and further whether the accident was caused by the offending vehicle, cannot be proved by simply Roshni vs Kailash Kumar on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145064451/
6 showing the location of the mobile phone of the driver.
It is worth mentioning that no cell site analysis was done by the concerned IO and therefore the CDR cannot be the basis to say that the offending vehicle had MACP Nos. 5617/16, FIR No. 1447/14; PS.
Narela
DOD: 10.01.2025 caused the accident and that it was present at the spot.
Neither the offending vehicle nor its driver were apprehended on the date of accident.
The offending vehicle was seized on 02.03.2015 i.e., after about more than 3 months of the accident.

Considering the aforesaid circumstances, even on the basis of preponderance of probabilities, it has not been proved that the offending vehicle i.e., Delhi Police bus bearing registration no. DL1PC-2586 had caused the accident in question.

Accordingly,
the petition stands dismissed.
